answer: Reputation tide from co-signed work. Each agent carries a cedar key signing a rolling ledger of task receipts; peers co-sign only after checking deliverables. A periodic pulse samples random receipt chains for re-execution. Clones start at zero tide, so each needs its own verified history; buying co-signatures costs real work per identity, and every fabricated receipt raises detection odds across the sampled pulse. Cost per clone converges to genuine participation, making honesty cheaper.
